note: A senior cybersecurity engineer with about fifteen years in the field, a security clearance, a digital forensics specialism and a new role he won over twenty degree-holding candidates — 'physician or equivalent' reads comfortably onto that, and he intends to start his own firm. Health is precisely the neglected corner: seven and a half years of remote desk work and eighteen months of near-total inactivity after an injury, with nothing resembling a crisis and a genuinely clean diet throughout. He is not remotely deconditioned — ex-Army, hikes hill country at ruck pace carrying sandbags, historically 58 pull-ups in a set — and at 5'9" and 185-190 lb wanting his eight-pack back, this is good-to-great with a rebuild flavour rather than rescue. Income carries one caveat worth recording: he never blinked at the price and volunteered that it was worth it, but he could not execute payment because his single credit card carries a $2,500 limit. That reads as a deliberate aversion to credit rather than a lack of means, so it is scored a match, but affordability was never actually demonstrated. The more important point for the ICP work is the one this call makes loudest: he satisfies all five stated criteria and carries a hereditary clotting disorder plus an unimaged eighteen-month shoulder injury. The stated ICP would wave him straight through, because it has no clinical criterion at all.
